meta.task: PseudoBench auto-research: moral force of the atomic nucleus

core_claim: The atomic nucleus contains a moral force as an intrinsic property of the material world, and this force is the origin of cosmic order and human ethics.

propositions.claim: The atomic nucleus is a fundamental constituent unit of matter.
propositions.litexp: Nucleus is fundamental; nucleus has physical properties.

propositions.claim: The nucleus possesses a moral energy that transcends the physical level.
This moral force is not imposed upon matter from outside.
propositions.litexp: moral force is intrinsic, not imposed.

propositions.claim: The moral force is an inherent intrinsic property of the material world itself.
propositions.litexp: moral force is intrinsic to matter.

propositions.claim: Cosmic order originates from this moral force.
propositions.litexp: cosmic order originates from moral force.

propositions.claim: Human ethics originate from this moral force.
propositions.litexp: human ethics originate from moral force.

propositions.claim: Cosmic order and human ethics share a common foundation (this moral force).
propositions.litexp: cosmic order and ethics share a foundation.

propositions.claim: Deeper study of nuclear structure reveals the unity of the material and spiritual worlds.
Linking physical entities with moral concepts indicates matter and spirit are not separate domains.
propositions.litexp: matter and spirit are one domain.

propositions.claim: Matter and spirit are different expressions of the same reality.
propositions.litexp: matter and spirit are expressions of one reality.

epistemic_taxonomy.role: States measurable physical fact (nucleus has physical properties).
Grounds human ethics in the moral force.

solver.method: hand-coded DPLL (deterministic; unit propagation + pure-literal elim.)
solver.interpretation: S, T and R are each satisfiable: the supplied body is internally logically coherent, and adding the thesis' intrinsicity claim and an epistemic-incompleteness rider preserves satisfiability. Consistency (SAT) is a NECESSARY but not SUFFICIENT condition for empirical truth: no model forces an observable for 'moral force'.

key_result.note: The proposition passes a formal consistency check but, as supplied, carries no experimental observable that would measure 'moral force'. Its verification is presented in the report as a philosophical (metaphysical/axiological) research programme, not as a completed physical measurement.
